messages:
maria: Heads up — us-east-1 inference-sidecars are hitting ephemeral port depletion, model pulls failing with ECONNRESET / connect timeouts since ~10:12 UTC.

james: Can you paste netstat/ss snippet and local port range?

maria: ```
$ ss -tan | grep TIME-WAIT | wc -l
34200
$ cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range
32768	60999
```

ankit: 34k TIME_WAIT is massive. Are sidecars opening a new TCP for every model pull? We should be reusing keepalives / connection pools.

laura: Any changes rolled recently to sidecar or fetch logic?

maria: No image change. We had scheduled model batch pulls and concurrency spiked x4. Sidecars open new outbound sockets per fetch.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-5234 - ephemeral-port depletion (us-east-1) :warning:

james: Short term mitigation: flip feature flag to reduce parallel model-pull concurrency to 4. Also nudge HPA to add nodes so ephemeral usage distributes.

maria: Pushed flag -> rolling update starting in 2m.

deploy-bot: Rollout started: inference-sidecar:v2.1.3 @ 1745254350

ankit: Another immediate option: deploy an egress-proxy to multiplex outbound model fetches through long-lived connections, reduces per-pod ephemeral usage. Might be faster than adding NAT capacity.

laura: We can also bump ip_local_port_range on the sidecars to widen ephemeral space (e.g. to 32768-61000 -> 1024-65535), but that's a bandaid. Will need kernel tweak and validation.

james: Increasing range buys time but doesn't fix connection churn. Long-term: connection reuse, egress multiplexing, or per-AZ NAT scaling + better spread.

maria: Rolling out sidecar rate-limiter to cap fetch concurrency per-pod now.

ops-bot: Dashboard: https://console/redwood/d/egress/ephemeral-ports?refresh=30s

ankit: Also check S3/model-store traffic — move to VPC endpoint to avoid NAT if possible. We've seen SNAT table saturation when many EIPs used.

laura: Quick repro: when ports are exhausted curl to model store returns 'curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer' or immediate connection reset.

james: After enabling the concurrency cap, TIME_WAIT dropped 34k -> 9.6k in ~7 minutes. Flag working as expected.

maria: Agreed. Next actions: 1) Keep concurrency flag on for 24h, 2) POC egress-proxy this week, 3) Infra: request temporary NAT capacity increase in us-east-1 AZ-a.

ankit: I'll open a cost ticket for temporary NAT capacity & EIP increase. Please add alert: TIME_WAIT > 20k.

laura: Add runbook note: if ephemeral > threshold, flip concurrency flag + scale nodes; avoid rebooting NAT as first step.

maria: Thanks — tagging @sre-oncall for follow-up tomorrow.

james: :thumbsup: Logging timeline and metrics in the incident ticket for postmortem.
